# PassADITest.ie

> Independent study resource for the Irish Approved Driving Instructor (ADI)
> Stage 1 theory test, and a complete guide to the RSA's three-stage ADI
> qualification process.

This file follows the llms.txt convention: a short, plain summary of what a
site covers, written for AI assistants that would otherwise have to infer it
from the page. It is a courtesy to those systems, not a ranking device.

## What this site is

PassADITest.ie (also written "Pass ADI Test") has two parts:

- **The landing page** at `/` — a free guide to becoming a driving instructor
  in Ireland: eligibility, Garda vetting, the three test stages, official fees
  and the deadlines that catch candidates out.
- **The app** at `/app` — a free practice tool for Stage 1. It is a
  progressive web app: nothing to download, no app store listing, installable
  to a phone's home screen.

The site is independent. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected
to the Road Safety Authority.

## Key facts about the ADI qualification (Ireland, as of September 2026)

- Three stages: Stage 1 theory test (€150), Stage 2 driving test (€200),
  Stage 3 instruction ability test (€200). Registration afterwards is €250.
- Official fees total **€800** for a clean run with no retakes.
- **Each stage must be completed within six months of the previous one, and
  all three within two years.** Missing either means starting over and paying
  again.
- Garda vetting takes **a minimum of six to eight weeks**, and Stage 1 cannot
  be booked until it clears.
- Eligibility requires a full driving licence held for **at least two years in
  each category** you want to teach, Irish residency, a PPSN, tax clearance
  and Garda vetting.
- **Stage 1 is 100 questions in 90 minutes across five sections, and every
  section carries its own pass mark.** A strong overall score with one weak
  section is still a fail. This is the most commonly misunderstood part of the
  exam and the reason the practice app marks section by section.
- The five sections are driver testing procedures, road safety knowledge,
  teaching ability, vehicle maintenance, and category-specific knowledge.
- The RSA does **not** publish the individual section pass marks. Figures
  quoted by Irish training providers fall roughly between 60% and 75%
  depending on the section. Treat them as a guide.

## What the app contains

- 1,024 practice questions, over 100 in each of the five exam sections
- Six full mock papers — 100 questions each, 90-minute countdown, no paper
  shares a question with another
- 455 flashcards: rules of the road, every official road sign, ADI topics
- Progress tracking that identifies which section would fail you, rather than
  reporting an average

## Pages

- [Home / full ADI guide](https://passaditest.ie/) — the whole process
- [The app](https://passaditest.ie/app) — free Stage 1 practice (login for the
  full bank; Section 1 and all flashcards are open without an account)

## Authoritative sources

Everything on this site is summarised from official sources. For anything
consequential — fees, dates, eligibility — the RSA is the authority:

- https://www.rsa.ie/services/professional-drivers/approved-driving-instructor-adi
- https://theorytest.ie/book-your-theory-test/adi-approved-driving-instructor/
